intuition.title: Why complementary spectroscopy?
intuition.summary: The authors motivate combined local-structure and ligand-sensitive measurements because the 1–2 nm cluster–nanocrystal transition and beam-sensitive wires challenge conventional diffraction/HRTEM. XAS/XPS probes core/local species; solution NMR probes ligand binding and exchange.
intuition.scope: Main-article rationale or author interpretation; SI is unverified.

intuition.title: Why a chain-based nanowire cross-section?
intuition.summary: The authors use bismuthinite’s anisotropic structure: stronger short Bi–S intrachain bonds along c and weaker interchain contacts; two proposed wire cross-sections preserve the former while cleaving along the latter. Bond-valence analysis favors the more homogeneous eight-chain model.
intuition.scope: Main-article rationale or author interpretation; SI is unverified.

intuition.title: Why propose Bi–N coordination?
intuition.summary: The measured first-shell Bi coordination exceeds the bulk reference value. The authors propose dative oleylamine coordination to accessible surface Bi sites; up to 75% are accessible in their preferred model. NMR/XPS show excess amine and fast exchange. Ligand occupancy is a proposed model rather than an atomic surface measurement.
intuition.scope: Main-article rationale or author interpretation; SI is unverified.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
